page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance tailored for compute-centric tasks that do not require extensive memory capacity. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed by KVM, the instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at 2.7 GHz. It allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading, paired with 16 GiB of RAM, translating to an exact 2.0 GiB per vCPU ratio. The processor integrates 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache pool. Advanced instruction extensions are available, including AVX-512 with VNNI and bfloat16, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

The instance profile omits local storage and GPU hardware, necessitating external cloud disks for all operating system and persistent data needs. Baseline networking throughput is provisioned at 4 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addressing. Synthetic benchmarks showcase strong single-thread efficiency, with stress-ng single-core reaching 3061.58 and Geekbench single-core scoring 2001.0, both placing in the top quartile of evaluated instances. Multi-core compute performance, represented by a Geekbench multi-core score of 7752.0 and PassMark CPU score of 14407.18, performs within average cohort tiers, reflecting linear scaling across its 4 physical cores.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency standpoint, the 1:2 memory-to-CPU distribution reduces infrastructure expense by eliminating unutilized memory overhead for CPU-heavy tasks. Workloads that depend heavily on per-thread execution speed or vector processing benefit directly from the modern Zen core architecture. Consequently, the ecs.c8a.2xlarge instance is well positioned for front-end web serving, continuous integration builds, compilation tasks, batch data transformation, and distributed application microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the AMD EPYC 9T24 processor running at a base clock of 2.7 GHz on the KVM hypervisor. Configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 16 GiB of system memory, the instance maintains a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX-512, VNNI, and BF16, alongside cryptographic acceleration instructions like AES and SHA-NI. The instance provides 4 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and includes no local instance storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage for persistent data. Benchmark metrics reflect strong single-core performance, placing stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core in the top quartile, while multi-core compute and throughput scores align with median tiers. By avoiding the overhead of surplus memory or dedicated storage, ecs.c8a.2xlarge delivers efficient CPU-bound execution for web servers, batch processing, application backends, and continuous integration pipelines.
